raspgrade.readme_text:
--- license: cc-by-nc-4.0 size_categories: - 1K ## 🏷️ Annotation Format Note that the annotations follow the YOLO instance segmentation format. Please refer to [this page](https://docs.ultralytics.com/datasets/segment/) for more info. ## 🧪 How to read and display examples ```python from datasets import load_dataset from PIL import Image, ImageDraw import numpy as np import random # --- Configuration --- DATASET_NAME = "FBK-TeV/RaspGrade" SAMPLE_INDEX = 0 # Index of the sample to visualize from the 'valid' split OUTPUT_IMAGE = 'annotated_hub_image_fixed_colors.png' ALPHA = 128 # Transparency level for masks # Define a color map for different classes CLASS_COLORS = { 0: (255, 0, 0, ALPHA), # Red 1: (0, 255, 0, ALPHA), # Green 2: (0, 0, 255, ALPHA), # Blue 3: (255, 255, 0, ALPHA), # Yellow 4: (255, 0, 255, ALPHA) # Magenta # Add more colors for other class IDs if needed } def convert_normalized_polygon_to_pixels(polygon_normalized, width, height): polygon_pixels = (np.array(polygon_normalized).reshape(-1, 2) * np.array([width, height])).astype(int).flatten().tolist() return polygon_pixels if __name__ == "__main__": try: dataset = load_dataset(DATASET_NAME) if 'valid' not in dataset: raise ValueError(f"Split 'valid' not found in dataset '{DATASET_NAME}'") valid_dataset = dataset['valid'] if SAMPLE_INDEX >= len(valid_dataset): raise ValueError(f"Sample index {SAMPLE_INDEX} is out of bounds for the 'valid' split (size: {len(valid_dataset)})") sample = valid_dataset[SAMPLE_INDEX] original_image = sample['image'].convert("RGBA") width, height = original_image.size mask = Image.new('RGBA', (width, height), (0, 0, 0, 0)) mask_draw = ImageDraw.Draw(mask, 'RGBA') labels = sample['labels'] if isinstance(labels, list): for annotation in labels: if len(annotation) > 4: # Assuming YOLO format includes class and polygon class_id = int(annotation[0]) polygon_normalized = np.array(annotation[1:]).astype(float).reshape(-1, 2).flatten().tolist() polygon_pixels = convert_normalized_polygon_to_pixels(polygon_normalized, width, height) color = CLASS_COLORS.get(class_id, (255, 255, 255, ALPHA)) # Default to white if class_id not in map mask_draw.polygon(polygon_pixels, fill=color) annotated_image = Image.alpha_composite(original_image, mask) annotated_image.save(OUTPUT_IMAGE) print(f"Annotated image with fixed colors saved as {OUTPUT_IMAGE}") annotated_image.show() except Exception as e: print(f"An error occurred: {e}") ``` ## 🙏 Acknowledgement

This work is supported by European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101092043, project AGILEHAND (Smart Grading, Handling and Packaging Solutions for Soft and Deformable Products in Agile and Reconfigurable Lines.

## 🤝 Partners
## 📖 Citation ```bibtex @article{mekhalfi2025raspgrade, title={The RaspGrade Dataset: Towards Automatic Raspberry Ripeness Grading with Deep Learning}, author={Mekhalfi, Mohamed Lamine and Chippendale, Paul and Poiesi, Fabio and Bonecher, Samuele and Osler, Gilberto and Zancanella, Nicola}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2505.08537}, year={2025} } ```

metadata.title: RaspGrade
metadata.description:
🍓 The RaspGrade Dataset: Towards Automatic Raspberry Ripeness Grading with Deep Learning

This research investigates the application of computer vision for rapid, accurate, and non-invasive food quality assessment, focusing on the novel challenge of real-time raspberry grading into five distinct classes within an industrial environment as the fruits move along a conveyor belt. To address this, a dedicated dataset of raspberries, namely RaspGrade, was acquired and meticulously annotated.

Instance segmentation experiments revealed that accurate fruit-level masks can be obtained; however, the classification of certain raspberry grades presents challenges due to color similarities and occlusion, while others are more readily distinguishable based on color.

root_geometry_admission.root_visual_review: Viewed all five corrected original/polygon pairs: TRAIN img001,img054,img107; author-valid img161,img200. Individual touching/occluded fruit outlines visibly reasonable. This samples annotations, not a claim every instance was manually reviewed.
root_geometry_admission.primary_semantics_review: Root read retained author paper Figure3: class0 is punnet, 1..5 are fruit grades. Actual 5043 fruit polygons excludes all 200 container polygons.
root_geometry_admission.geometry_policy: Author classes1..5: one tight bounding box per individual polygon, app class4 Fruit_grade_unknown; exclude class0. No maturity/species claims or semantic-union instance guessing.
root_geometry_admission.author_split_policy: Exact TRAIN160/4042 fruit and author-valid40/1001 fruit. No random resplit; no physical-family IDs are available. Author valid/testing terminology and unknown cross-split physical independence retained.
root_geometry_admission.license_restriction: DATA AND ANY RESULTING MODEL NONCOMMERCIAL DEMO ONLY. Follow stricter author HF CC-BY-NC-4.0; retain conflicting Zenodo CC-BY-4.0 record and separate article notice. No commercial-use clearance claimed.
root_geometry_admission.permitted_next_action: Build and test an isolated geometry-only manifest/cache; no live-app asset change. Root reviews new training recipe and prepared inputs before a single finite fit.
root_geometry_admission.user_video_policy: Supplied conveyor video and its45GT remain outside training, augmentation, calibration, checkpoint and threshold selection.

source_review.primary_class_semantics_evidence: Author paper Figure 3 and Table I; observed label frequencies exactly match each class
source_review.geometry_conversion_if_later_admitted: Only 1..5 fruit polygons -> per-author-instance tight boxes -> class4 Fruit_grade_unknown; discard class0; never transfer grade labels
source_review.physical_grouping: Paper describes 200 punnets. Parquet has image_id only, no punnet/session/recording/camera/batch identifiers; unique physical berries or independence across splits cannot be established.
source_review.split_disclosure: HF publishes train160/valid40 in sequential image IDs. Paper calls the latter testing in prose but Validation in Table I; preserve exact author membership and disclose ambiguity, no random resplit.

source_review.visual_review: Subagent viewed all five corrected original/polygon pairs. Industrial punnets of multiple touching/occluded raspberries, morphology unlike mango conveyor; not proof of target performance. Root must independently admit annotations.

duplicate_check.limitation: Exact encoded-byte comparison only; no decoded user-video access, perceptual dedupe or inference. Five reviewed samples visibly differ from previously reviewed mango recording; near-duplicate/session leakage is not established.
